Subject: Clarification: evidence access model and export expectations (HarborGroup RFP)

Markus,

Thanks for taking our RFP. We have a couple of follow-ups specifically around audit/evidence availability that we need to confirm before progressing to the technical evaluation:

1) For large-scale requests (30TB+ of audit data) do you support a live query export (incremental slice with resume tokens) or do you always do a point-in-time snapshot?
2) What is your default manifest/hash model for proving chain-of-custody? Is SHA256 + signed manifest provided?
3) What deliverable formats do you support for exports (ndjson, parquet, CSV) and do you provide schema maps?
4) Typical SLA for export fulfillment and sample timelines for large exports (30TB on S3, encrypted in transit) — we need a baseline for contractual language.

Attached is a short excerpt from our procurement team; we'll follow-up with the official redline request. Can we schedule a short call tomorrow to review?

Appreciate it,
Emily

Emily — thanks, got the RFP excerpt. I looped in Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (security & compliance) so you have technical and delivery context. High level answers below; Marissa will follow with the cryptographic and manifest specifics.

- Live query vs snapshot: Redwood supports both. For latency-sensitive, incremental exports we expose a resumable export API (cursor-based) that lets you continue harvesting from a consistent logical timeline. For forensic/legal handoffs we recommend a cryptographic point-in-time snapshot with an immutable manifest.
- Hashing & manifest: we provide SHA256 digests per file and a signed manifest (timestamped by our KMS-backed signing service).
- Formats: ndjson and parquet supported natively; CSV for smaller slices. We also publish a schema map for each export bundle.
- SLA & timelines: typical fulfillment for a 30TB bulk export to an S3 bucket (customer-provided) is 5–10 business days depending on routing and throttles; incremental exports are available in hours depending on slice size. We'll provide a formal export SLA you can include in the MSA.

I've attached our current export spec and a sample manifest schema for your review. Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow 11:00–11:30 PT?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Emily — digging into the technical specifics you asked for. Below is an excerpt we typically provide in RFP responses; happy to expand into a short appendix for your procurement/forensics folks.

1) Incremental export durability: our resumable export API emits opaque resume tokens scoped to the export job. Tokens are persisted for a customer-configurable window (default 90 days). Tokens are checkpointed to a durable store; you can pause and resume without gaps within the retention window. For longer-term harvesting we recommend scheduled snapshot exports.

2) Manifest & signing: we generate a per-export manifest with entries for each object: {file_path, sha256_hex, size_bytes, sequence_offset}. The manifest itself is hashed and then signed using our KMS-backed key (customer-blinded signing option available for higher assurance). The signed manifest includes an RFC3339 timestamp and a signing key id.

3) Tamper evidence & QA: our export SLA timelines include a verification pass — we compute and verify hashes during transfer, provide a signed verification report, and produce a chain-of-custody report that lists who requested the export and what system job IDs were used. For your 30TB example we break the job into N concurrent shards; each shard produces its own manifest and a top-level aggregator manifest (hierarchical hashing) so you can verify per-shard and global integrity.

4) Formats & schema: ndjson (line-delimited JSON) is our primary forensic format (schema versioned). Parquet is offered for analytics exports. We attach a schema map (field -> description, type, example) with every bundle.

5) Delivery & encryption: exports are delivered to a customer S3 bucket via multipart encrypted transfer (TLS + server-side encryption optional). We can also upload to a temporary encrypted staging bucket and provide presigned URLs for retrieval. Post-delivery we keep a sealed copy internally for 30 days for re-provisioning if needed (configurable).

6) SLA & timelines: door-to-door for a 30TB export (includes QA & verification, manifest signing, and delivery to customer S3) — target 7 business days under standard throughput profiles. If you need an accelerated timeline we offer a premium expedited pipeline (3 business days) as an addendum.

Sample snippet (manifest topology):
```
{
  "manifest_version": "1.2",
  "export_id": "exp-20261012-001",
  "signed": true,
  "files": [
    {"path": "audit/2026-09-01/part-0001.ndjson.gz", "sha256": "a3f1...", "size": 104857600},
    {"path": "audit/2026-09-01/part-0002.ndjson.gz", "sha256": "b9c2...", "size": 104857600}
  ],
  "aggregate_sha256": "c4d2...",
  "signed_by": "redwood-export-signer-v1",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-12T21:15:03Z"
}
```
I'll attach the manifest JSON sample and a short checklist for verification. If you want HSM-signed timestamps we can engage the crypto team to provide an attestation.

—Marissa
